summary: Galsang Gomboev worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied under Józef Szczepan Kowalewski and taught Mongolian at Saint Petersburg State University from 1855 to 1863.

Gananath Obeyesekere specialized in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Peradeniya and University of Washington, and held posts at the University of Ceylon, University of Washington, UC San Diego, and Princeton University (1980–2000).

Ganesh Prasad was a scholar in history and archaeology who studied at the universities of Allahabad and Calcutta. He served as head of department at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1905) and held posts at Banaras Hindu University and the University of Calcutta.

Ganganatha Jha worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Calcutta, Allahabad, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit universities, he was Sanskrit professor at Muir Central College (1902–1918), principal of Sanskrit College (1918), and Vice-Chancellor of Allahabad University (1923–1932).

Gangzhun is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Qinghai Nationalities University and earned a master's degree from Northwest Minzu University (1998–2001) under the supervision of Alak Dorje Rinpoche.

Ganzorig Davaa-Ochir is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed an M.Phil in Tibetan Studies at the University of Oslo under Hanna Havnevik (attested 2008) and also studied under Lama Byambaa.
Garab Dorje Rinpoche is a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He pursued traditional studies under Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje and Thinley Norbu Rinpoche.

Garcin de Tassy was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Collège de France under Silvestre de Sacy and Jean-Daniel Kieffer. He held a chair in Indian languages at INALCO/École des langues orientales (~1828–1878) and directed the Société Asiatique.

Gareth Fisher is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He completed a Ph.D. at the University of Virginia in 2006 and held a post as Assistant Professor of Religion and Anthropology at Syracuse University (attested 2011–2016).

Gareth Sparham specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at McGill University, the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, and under Ashok Aklujkar at the University of British Columbia (Ph.D.), later teaching Tibetan language at the University of Michigan (1999–2009).

Gary A. Tubb is an Indologist who studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He held faculty and teaching appointments at Harvard University (attested 1999), Columbia University (attested 2007), and the University of Chicago (attested 2011).

Gary D. DeAngelis works in religious and Buddhist studies. Mentored by Masatoshi Nagatomi, George Rupp, W. J. Johnson, Herbert Mason, and Muhammad Daud Rahbar, he served as Associate Director of the Center for Interdisciplinary Studies at the College of the Holy Cross.

Gary Snyder is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at Reed College, Indiana University, and UC Berkeley under Shih-Hsiang Chen, later serving as a professor at the University of California, Davis from 1986 to 2002.

Gary Urton is an archaeologist and historian who studied at Eastern New Mexico University, the University of New Mexico, and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. He taught at Colgate University (1978–2002) and held an endowed professorship at Harvard University (2012–2020).

Gaspare Gorresio was an Indologist who studied at the University of Turin and under Eugène Burnouf and Stanislas Julien. He held the chair in Sanskrit at Turin (1852) and served as librarian and director of Turin's royal and university libraries.

Gaston Paris was a linguist who studied under Friedrich Christian Diez and at the École des chartes. He held major academic posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1869–1895) and the Collège de France (1872–1903).
Gaston Renondeau was a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who completed his education at the École Polytechnique around 1899 to 1901.
Gaton Ngawang Lekpa was an active figure in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Gauri Viswanathan is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She studied at the University of Delhi and Columbia University, taught English at the University of Delhi (~1973–1975), and became a professor and South Asia Institute director at Columbia University (~1989).

Gavin D'Costa works in religious studies. After studying at the universities of Birmingham and Cambridge, he taught at the West London Institute of Higher Education and held the post of Professor of Catholic Theology at the University of Bristol from 1993.
